chapter.title: Of A Wonderland
chapter.outline:
Jump to their first steps in heaven 133. The mulchers and Gneiss march through the first hell. Darkness, but with some shiny color to it, as though they descent into a pool of liquid opal, ankle-deep water too blue, walls made up of angles and shadows - and even the mulchers and gneiss take on different looks. (*Deep eyeshadow, all their gestures and words are overly-expressive, like they have been dropped into a German Expressionist silent movie*). Kallus's warnings from Chapter 2 are made real. *"I have always felt that the space of the basement was more than it promised to be." (Gneiss Line)*
Within minutes their stealthy approach is lost; a door handle shrieks like a dying goat as they turn it; Creatures Electric attack from all sides. The mulchers fight back with their replicas, and an intense, room-to-room, corridor-to-corridor battle ensures. A Mr. Montag (*Flying whales; their call is like an air-raid siren; when prodded, their calls can shatter glass, light filaments, and bones*) flies into view; two mulchers fall, instantly slain, bones cracked, while others cover their ears in time to recieve only hearing damage.
Gneiss ghosts ahead to scout for the path back up-stairs, but as he sees them ahead, the Butler sees him by the one sense he left unhidden, the secret, unnamed seventh. (*The butler speaks in a tender, almost loving/adoring voice - think Hisoka from Hunter X Hunter, or Lord Arioch from the Elric stories*). Outmatched, knowing he cannot defeat a butler, gneiss hears its mocking admission: disguised as the mulchers' housecat, it stole a set of their spellbreaker keys, broke the seals on the stairs, and allowed the creatures to enter - all in the name of chaos and "fun". The butler and Gneiss talk for some time; the names of other powerful butlers *(Julio, arluck, pick others)* are dropped. Gneiss parleys silence for safe passage, offering not to reveal its secret, if it will only let them go by unscathed.
But just then the mulchers arrive, Phansy fires on instinct, and the deal breaks. The butler slaughters them, the creatures attack from behind, and at the end, of eighteen demons and she-demons, only Gneiss walks away, activating his coat (*all 7 senses this time*). Joiyuss's death hit Gneiss hardests. Yet Gneiss still keeps the Axe and - still with Perli in his thoughts - proceeds further into hell, not out.
Some hours pass, as Gneiss puts time and distance between himself and the massacre. He cannot seem to find a Way - all paths look the same. Describe a vivid, grotesque travel sequence through hell - loopy pathways curling and through a jagged, sharp landscape, constantly shifting between uphills and steep declines, sometimes even running vertically up walls, or across the roop, like ribbons; none of it green, clean shag, but covered in a powder that isn't dirt, like fine white chalk, while cliffs and crags merge indistinguishable with a shale-colored ceiling. (*Describe one section like follows: Gneiss striding through library of server lockers, or racks, behind grated fencing; a datacenter, but frame it from eyes of medieval scholastic*).
After climbing up a path through an increasingly-narrow gorge of rocks sharp enough to cut paper (but not the Coat), gneiss encounters a Moon with a Face, set directly into a wall of solid jade stone, hidden under a shadow of two intertwined, dead, weeping-willow trees - it is a talking mutant door of crescent shape. (*Through dialogue, give a vivid depiction of the door's personality - have it talk like Werner Herzog*) The door asks five logic-puzzle questions (*specify the exact questions, in dialogue*), one after the other, and ignores gneiss when he presses it to tell him what it wants, or why it's asking, or to respond in any way. Gneiss, having answered all (some right, some wrong), gives up ("A brain of me will not waste more time in such fencings."); instead of blasting the door, he decides to spare it. In thanks, the Moon with a Face creaks open a forgotten hallway, and asks to be remembered.
context: The protagonist is Gneiss Rong, a drifter.
The story is told in first-person, past tense.
Gneiss is descending into hell to rescue Sirrel, his love.
His Coat hides him from all seven senses.
All humans are demons; women are she-demons.

blobs.prompt: Write a chunk of prose about the first steps into the first hell: darkness with a shine to it, ankle-deep water too blue to be water, walls built of angles and shadow, like wading into liquid opal.
blobs.text:
The Coat drank the light, hiding me from all seven senses, but it couldn't mute the sound of my own boots. Thirteen steps down, the air thickening to a bruise-purple pressure. The water rose over my ankles, too blue to be water—cobalt, glacial, glowing with a luminous spirit-wraith shimmer that threw my shadow long and jagged against the walls.

Walls built of angles and shadow, leaning inward like a mouth full of broken teeth. I waded into liquid opal, the cold biting through leather soles. Ahead, five gothic stone archways yawned in sequence, each keystone carved with a weeping she-demon, their stone tears frozen mid-fall. The first hell smelled of ozone and old iron. Sirrel was deeper. She had to be.

blobs.prompt: Describe how the descending light changes the marchers themselves, deepening the eyes of the mulchers and of Gneiss, stretching every gesture and every spoken word into something enormous and staged.
tags: Grounding Detail: The Gratuitous Detail: details with no plot or thematic function.
blobs.text:
The light did not fall so much as congeal, thickening around us like bruised amethyst. It caught the mulchers first — their eyes deepening into wet, black pits that seemed to drink the gloom, pupils widening until irises vanished. My own vision sharpened in answer, the Coat's weave humming against my thin wiry frame as the descent stretched my shadow into something portentous and long.

A mulcher scratched his jaw. The gesture unfolded in slow silence, enormous, staged — fingers dragging through beard-stubble like a ritual. Another spat. The arc of spittle hung suspended, catching the strange light, a gratuitous detail: a fleck of mica in the sludge, glowing briefly before vanishing. Words dragged. "Move," someone said, and the syllable elongated, vowels flattening into something liturgical. Boots on basalt became percussion. Breath became wind.

The grounding detail settled in my palm: the Coat's collar, stiff with old salt and older blood, chafing my neck with every deliberate turn of my head. Down here, nothing was casual. Everything was ceremony. Everything was watched.

blobs.prompt: Render the moment Kallus's old warnings prove true, and let Gneiss admit aloud that he has always felt the basement was more than the space it promised to be.
tags: Grounding Detail: Traces of Human Agency.
blobs.text:
“I told the dark what I’d never confessed,” I said aloud. “Kallus warned me this basement was more than the space it promised to be. He was right—I always felt it.”

My voice died in the primal dark land, smothered by the plain of silence that stretched beyond all reckoning.

Yet traces of human agency lingered: rusted hooks driven into stone, a child’s shoe fused to ash, sigils scratched in a tongue I almost recognized. Proof that others had descended and failed to name what waited below.

My Coat hid me from all seven senses, but it could not dull the dread unfurling in my gut. The anticipation coiled like a she-demon’s smile—sharp, knowing, patient. I was in hell’s mouth now, and Sirrel was somewhere deeper in its throat.

blobs.prompt: Show the stealth collapsing all at once: a door handle turned, and the sound it makes going through the corridor like a goat dying.
blobs.text:
The Coat kept me null, a hole in the world where the seven senses found no purchase. I moved through the torch-lit prison corridor, smoke stinging eyes I didn't dare open wide, timing my steps to the drips echoing from the abyssal darkness ahead. Sirrel’s cell was close. I could taste the sulfur on her breath.

I reached the heavy iron door, fingers brushing the cold latch. **Action:** I turned the handle, slow as glacial melt, the mechanism whispering on grease I’d prayed would hold.

**Complication / Obstacle:** The grounding pin sheared with a *snap* loud as a whip-crack. The handle didn't turn; it *screamed*, a raw, tearing metal shriek that didn't just hang in the air—it propagated. It bounced off the damp stones, gained throat, and rolled down the corridor like a goat dying, wet and ragged and utterly final. The torch flames didn't flicker; they leaned toward the sound. Somewhere deep in the dark, a she-demon’s head snapped up, nostrils flaring, tasting the sudden, violent hole in the silence where I stood.

blobs.prompt: Narrate the Creatures Electric arriving from every side at once, out of the angles and the shallow blue water, faster than the party can form a line.
tags: Grounding Detail: Procedural Authority: jargon, deliberate misuse of tools, etc.
blobs.text:
The water wasn't deep — ankle-deep brine over cracked basalt, the kind the survey boys called *littoral shelf, Class IV, non-navigable*. I'd repurposed the sounding lead as a bludgeon, wrapping the line around my wrist until the lead weight kissed my knuckles. Good procedure. Bad tool. The Coat kept me ghost-cold against the seven senses, but the party behind me didn't wear Coats.

Kael's vox-caster sputtered *contact front* and *flank speed* in the same breath. Joren tried to pivot the formation into a firing wedge, boots slipping on the biofilm.

They came from the angles. Not the water — the *angles*. The geometry of the place folded wrong, and the Creatures Electric unfolded out of the fold: needle-jawed, bioluminescent, trailing voltage like sick halos. They didn't swim. They *translated*.

Three heartbeats. The line never formed.

Joren's vox-caster arched into the brine, still screaming *tactical advance* as the water boiled blue around his knees. Kael fired into the swarm, rounds flashing to steam. A Garthim — hulking, chitinous, wrong-legged — rose from the shallows behind them, mandibles clicking *target acquired* in a voice like grinding tectonic plates.

The Coat hid me. It didn't hide the sound of feeding.

blobs.prompt: Write a chunk about the mulchers answering with their replicas, and the fight that follows: room to room, corridor to corridor, no ground held longer than a breath.
tags: Grounding Detail: Sensory / Textural: Color, temperature, grain, sound, smell.
blobs.text:
The mulchers answered with replicas—wet, breathing things stripped from my own memory. Sirrel’s face on a thing with too many joints. My mother’s voice from a throat full of grinding stone. They came boiling out of the fiend-haunted cavern depths, smelling of ozone and old copper.

I didn’t parley. The Coat swallowed my heat, my scent, the very sound of my marrow, but the replicas didn’t need senses. They needed only the order to mulch.

Action became combat in a heartbeat. I drove the spike-handled shiv through the first replica’s collarbone, feeling the grain of false bone crunch like frost-bitten gravel. Hot, black ichor sprayed my knuckles. I kicked the corpse into the second, buying a second of floor space.

Room to room. Corridor to corridor. No ground held longer than a breath. A she-demon replica unhinged her jaw to scream a frequency that liquefied the air; I ruptured her eardrums with a palm strike and took her lungs with the follow-through. The stone walls wept condensation, cold as a butcher’s slab against my shoulders. I moved like a valiant trencherman clearing a sump, shoveling meat aside, deeper, always deeper, the taste of iron thick in my throat.

blobs.prompt: Describe a Mr. Montag coming into view above the fighting, a whale flying without water, its call opening across the hall like an air-raid siren.
tags: Grounding Detail: Embodiment: Characters physical quirks.
blobs.text: I kept low beneath the Coat, its fabric swallowing my heat, my scent, the tremor in my left hand that never stopped shaking. The hall was all teeth and she-demons tearing at each other, red silhouettes screaming in a language that tasted like iron. Then the fighting parted like water before a blade, and Mr. Montag came into view above it, a whale flying without water, his bulk blotting the black ceiling. His voice—loud, booming—opened across the hall like an air-raid siren, shaking the marrow in my crooked spine. He wore a cloak of living shadow, a cloaked nocturnal terror; one arm ended in a hooked claw that dragged behind him, an old physical quirk of violence, while his other fist clutched a chain of broken teeth. I pressed my palm to my stuttering heart, hidden from all seven senses, and knew Sirrel was closer.

blobs.prompt: Show what the call does when it lands: two mulchers dropped where they stand with their bones cracked through, and the others saved only by hands clapped over their ears, and saved only partly.
tags: Grounding Detail: Sensory / Textural: Color, temperature, grain, sound, smell.
blobs.text:
The Call didn’t echo; it *settled*, a wet weight pressing against the flagstones of the death-pervaded-room. I watched the air shimmer, thick as hot tallow, smelling of sulfur and old iron.

Two mulchers simply ceased to stand. Their bones didn't break so much as *dissolve*, the white powder puffing out through skin the color of raw dough. They hit the grain of the floor in heaps of steaming meat, silence swallowing their screams before the sound could birth.

The others reacted on instinct, claws clamping over ear-holes, scales rattling against horn. It saved them from the liquefaction, but only partly. Blood, black and thick as tar, bubbled from between their fingers, tracking hot paths down wrists the color of bruised plums. They remained upright, trembling, their throats working around silent retching, equilibrium shattered by a frequency that tasted of copper and rot.

My Coat drank the vibration, leaving me cold and untouched in the sudden, ringing quiet.

Then the she-demons at the back—the ones with the barbed whips—stopped clutching their heads and started grinning. They had located the source. They had located *me*.

blobs.prompt: Narrate Gneiss slipping away from the battle under his Coat, hidden and unheard, scouting ahead for the path that leads back up the stairs.
tags: Grounding Detail: Particularity: A specific detail.
blobs.text:
I slipped from the battle as my Coat drank the clamor—no shape, no stench, not even a tremor in the seventh sense. The demons, every one of them human in some ruined form, hacked at shadows; the she-demons shrieked with voices like breaking glass. I moved unseen, scouting ahead for the stair that climbed back toward Sirrel.

The corridor spilled into the nether-adytum. There I stopped.

An obsidian-eyed she-demon lay collapsed against a pillar, her throat torn by something that had left no footprints. In her dead grip was a scrap of parchment—Sirrel’s hand—bearing one particularity: a hairline fracture drawn across the seventh stair, the exact spot where the ascent turned left into smoke.

The path up was real. But she had died marking it.

blobs.prompt: Render the moment the Butler turns and finds him anyway, taking him by the one sense Gneiss left uncovered, the secret and unnamed seventh.
blobs.text:
The Coat drank the light, swallowed the heat, muted the clatter of my boots on the obsidian stairs. I was a ghost in the machine of Hell, invisible to the six senses the Church teaches—sight, sound, scent, touch, taste, and the magnetic pull of the soul. I passed the Guardian Statues, their eyes hollowed out and stuffed with praying fingers, a Grounding Detail: Cultural Artifacts left by the First Fallen to mark the boundary. The air thickened into a bodiless cosmic void, pressing against the leather, testing the seams.

I reached the landing. The Butler stood by the iron door, polishing a silver tray with a rag of human skin. His back was turned. I drew the knife, silent as a held breath. Life-in-death states shimmered around us, the trapped souls vibrating in the walls.

I struck.

The blade kissed the vertebrae. The Butler did not fall. He turned, the motion fluid, impossible, his face a smooth mask of polished bone. He hadn't heard the leather creak. He hadn't smelled the copper on my breath. He smiled, tapping the side of his lipless mouth—the organ for the secret, unnamed seventh sense: *Intent*.

"You're late, Drifter," he whispered, the sound bypassing my ears to hammer directly against my spine. "She expected you to try the front door."

blobs.prompt: Write a chunk about how the Butler speaks to Gneiss: tender, adoring, delighted, and about Gneiss understanding immediately that a butler is not a thing he can beat.
tags: Grounding Detail: Wear and Accumulated Time.
blobs.text:
"You've kept the stitching tight, Master Rong. Seventy-three years of dust and blood, and not a fray at the cuff." The Butler’s voice was velvet over gravel, adoration leaking from every syllable. He polished a silver tray that hadn't held a drink in decades, his gloves worn thin at the fingertips by generations of service. "She waits in the Ninth Circle. She *always* waits."

My hand drifted to the hilt behind my hip, the Coat rippling to swallow the motion from the seven senses. Venom trailed from the blade’s edge, hissing on the obsidian floor.

"I'll carve a path through the Pit's own throat to reach her," I said, the threat tasting of ash and old iron. "Stand aside."

The Butler didn't flinch. He smiled, a expression of delighted ruin, haunted by a mortality he had long since negotiated away. "Oh, sir. One does not *beat* a Butler. One simply settles the bill."

blobs.prompt: Show the Butler confessing its game with pleasure: it wore the shape of the mulchers' housecat, stole their spellbreaker keys, broke the seals on the stairs, and let the creatures in for fun.
tags: Grounding Detail: Procedural Authority: jargon, deliberate misuse of tools, etc.
blobs.text:
"You're enjoying this," I said. My fingers found the seam in my Coat's collar—habit, not need. The Kevlar-weave hid me from all seven senses, but old muscle memory died hard.

The Butler's smile stretched too wide for a human face. Teeth clicked. "Protocol 9-C forbids deception during audit, drifter. I *am* the audit."

"Then audit this." I tossed the signet ring onto the basalt ledger-stone. It rang like a tuning fork. "Mulcher cell, Sector 4. You wore their housecat for three weeks. Panther-gait on the stairs—deliberate misuse of Form 7, Article 12. You stole the spellbreaker keys from the matriarch's sleep-pouch."

"Borrowed." A purr vibrated through the threshold's membrane. "The seals on Stair 13 were *bureaucratic error*. I merely corrected the paperwork."

"You broke them. Let the hunger-creatures in. For fun."

"Amusement is a valid metric under Clause 44." Its pupils dilated, vertical and gold. "The she-demons screamed beautifully. Sirrel's voice had a particular timbre when the mulchers dragged her down."

My hand closed on the ring. The Coat's hood whispered against my jaw.

"Keep talking," I said. "I'm recording every syllable for the Tribunal."

"There is no Tribunal. Only the stairs. And I hold the keys."

blobs.prompt: Narrate the conversation stretching on, the Butler naming others of its kind, Julio and Arluck among them, speaking of them the way one speaks of beloved rivals.
blobs.text:
The Butler polished a silver salver with a sleeve worn thin at the cuff, the cloth catching on the etched sigils of the First City—geometric spirals no living hand could replicate. We sat in the vestibule of the Seventh Gate, the air thick with the scent of ozone and old iron, while the conversation stretched thin and long as a tripwire.

"Julio keeps the Ledger of Ash," the Butler said, voice dry as crushed bone. "He counts the cinders of the oath-bound before they cool. Meticulous. Pedantic. I despise his precision."

He set the salver down, picking up a tarnished censer instead, turning it over to reveal a maker’s mark: a weeping eye.

"And Arluck tends the Garden of Silent Bells. He prunes the tongues of liars so they bloom only once a year. Cruelty disguised as horticulture. I envy his patience."

He spoke of them the way one speaks of beloved rivals—intimate, weary, fond. Names carved into the same foundation stones of a lost civilization. They were the other fingers on the fist that squeezed this world.

"Neither wears a Coat like yours, Drifter," he added, not looking up. "They cannot hide from the Seven Senses. They simply *endure* being seen."

blobs.prompt: Write the parley: Gneiss offering his silence about the keys, the seals, and the cat, in exchange for his party being let past unharmed.
tags: Grounding Detail: Traces of Human Agency.
blobs.text:
"You know what I carry," I said, voice flat in the deep-dwelling silence beyond the brazen-gateway. "Keys. Seals. The cat that watches the threshold."

The thing on the other side—tall, skin stitched from shadows, eyes like coals banked for morning—didn't move. Didn't breathe. Its fingers, however, twitched toward the hilt at its hip. A trace of human agency, that. Old habits dying harder than the flesh.

"Knowledge has weight," it rasped. "Price."

"My silence has more." I adjusted the Coat's collar, feeling the familiar shiver as it settled across the seven senses. "I walk past. My party walks past. Unharmed. Unmarked. In exchange, the keys stay lost, the seals stay broken, and the cat stays sleeping. You tell no one I was here. I tell no one you let us pass."

A long pause. Coal-eyes flickered.

"She-demons hunt in packs," it said finally. "Your woman. She smells of salt and treachery."

"Sirrel hunts alone," I corrected. "And she's not yours to name."

The thing's lipless mouth stretched—something like a smile, something like a wound. "Past the third circle, drifter. No further guarantee."

"Wouldn't dream of asking."

blobs.prompt: Render the arrival of the mulchers at the worst moment, and Phansy firing on instinct before anyone can speak, and the bargain breaking in that instant.
tags: Grounding Detail: Economic Texture: Cost, scarcity, counterfeits, etc.
blobs.text:
The counterfeit coin lay spread across the rust table—three clipped souls, barely tender for Sirrel’s ransom in a market where scarcity made even breath expensive. The she-demon leaned in, her claw hovering to seal the bargain. My Coat was drawn tight; not one of the seven senses could locate me.

Then the grate shattered.

The mulchers came up—four of them in patched leather, wielding dented scythes bought cheap from the war-ruins, volatile tools for desperate work. The worst possible moment.

Phansy fired on instinct.

Her pistol was counterfeit too—black-market powder cheap enough to blow her grip—but the blast caught the nearest mulcher in the throat. Before anyone could speak, the bargain broke like dry bone. The she-demon recoiled, screaming that my hidden silence had ruined her, never knowing the Coat had kept me invisible all along, or that Phansy’s reckless, desperate shot had just driven Sirrel’s price beyond any clipped soul I possessed.

blobs.prompt: Show the Butler killing them, unhurried and affectionate about it, moving through the mulchers as though performing a courtesy.
blobs.text:
I crouched behind the gilded-sarcophagus, my Coat deadening all seven senses; not one she-demon or demon-brother sensed my presence. The Butler approached the mulchers—thirteen in number, though only five still twitched—unhurried, affectionate, moving among them as though performing a courtesy. He cupped three throats, kissed seven brows, and they collapsed with gratitude. He was blood-drinking then, lapping from eleven wounds with a tender, nine-beat rhythm, each swallow a benediction. I remained unseen.

Then came the ritual. I carved nine sigils into the marble and spoke the Coat’s hidden name—once, then three times—binding my intent to rescue Sirrel from the lower dark. The spell drank my own blood in exchange: five drops, then seven, then one. Hell forgot me entirely. The Butler turned away, still smiling, and I slipped past the dead toward her.

blobs.prompt: Describe the Creatures Electric coming in from behind at the same time, and the end of it: of eighteen demons and she-demons, one left standing.
tags: Grounding Detail: Economic Texture: Cost, scarcity, counterfeits, etc.
blobs.text:
The Creatures Electric didn’t walk; they arced, jagged stripes of divine lightning given flesh and hunger, closing from the rear where the thermal vents blinded the Coat’s weave. I smelled ozone and scorched sulfur before the proximity alarms screamed in my teeth. Eighteen demons and she-demons fanned out, a semi-circle of horns and filed teeth, blocking the fissure to the Ninth Circle.

I didn’t draw the revolver. Bullets cost three grams of refined salt each—currency I couldn't waste on chaff. I dropped the counterfeit amulet I’d bartered for at the Styx crossing, the one supposedly blessed by a forgotten saint. It shattered against the basalt, a cheap glass fake bought with the last of my water ration. The fraud bought me a second of hesitation from the front rank.

A second was the Coat’s recharge cycle.

I spun inside the lightning’s embrace. The blade didn't cut; it *deleted*. Meat cauterized instantly, silent as a ledger balanced. The air thickened with the smell of burnt copper and the specific, sweet rot of she-demon hair. They fell like toppled idols, twitching once before the ground drank them.

The lightning faded. The Coat cooled.

One she-demon remained standing, her wings folded, clutching a ledger of souls. She checked the tally, unimpressed, and tapped a claw against the final entry: *Mine*.

blobs.prompt: Narrate Gneiss activating the Coat against all seven senses this time, and walking out of the room alone through what remains.
tags: Grounding Detail: Embodiment: Characters physical quirks.
blobs.text: My left hip hitched—old break never set right—as I pulled the Coat closed, and it swallowed all seven. Sight died: my shadow choked. Sound, the drip of blood, went mute; smell, the iron reek of landstrider slaughter, dissolved; taste, copper fear on my tongue, vanished; touch, cold on my scarred collarbone, erased; balance, my crooked spine straightening into absence; and that seventh pull toward Sirrel, silenced dead. I existed only inside the grayly illumined dread, stepping through she-demon remains—torn harness, glistening limbs like wet slate—where the landstriders lay in pieces. The room was ruin and dull, wall-born ash-light. I moved without ripple, alone, and walked out through what remained.

blobs.prompt: Write a chunk about the grief that follows, and how it is Joiyuss's death, above all the others, that reaches him.
tags: Grounding Detail: Wear and Accumulated Time.
collapsing boundaries between time and space
blobs.text:
The grief didn't hit like a blow. It settled, a sediment in the marrow, deposited by the Wear and Accumulated Time stitched into the Coat’s collar—frayed threads, the grease of a hundred hells, the dust of Sirrel’s bedroom window back when the world still turned right.

I have killed she-demons by the score. I have watched their mask-like pale visages shatter, felt the wet heat of their ending. Nothing stuck. They were obstacles, geometry to be navigated.

Joiyuss was different. Joiyuss who laughed at the sulfur vents. Joiyuss who shared his water skin when mine ran dry, his fingers brushing mine—human contact, ungloved, unguarded.

He died three days back. Or three centuries. The boundaries between time and space collapse down here; his final breath echoes in the same instant as the first step I took onto the obsidian slope.

I reach for the Coat’s clasp, needing the wool against my cheek, needing the smell of him caught in the fibers—sweat, cheap tobacco, the sharp mineral tang of the deep rock. My fingers close on nothing but cold air.

The Coat hides me from the seven senses of the Pit. It does not hide me from the memory of his hand in mine, nor the silence where his laugh used to live. That silence is the only thing louder than the screams.

blobs.prompt: Show Gneiss keeping the Axe, holding Perli in his thoughts, and choosing to go further down instead of back toward the stairs.
tags: Grounding Detail: Particularity: A specific detail.
blobs.text: I kept the axe. The hairline crack in its black iron head—thin as a she-demon’s smile—caught no light, but I knew it was there, running like a vein toward the eye where the hickory met steel. I had wrapped the grip in copper wire stripped from a lantern in the third circle, and my palm remembered the cold of it. Behind me, the stairs climbed back toward breath and noise, a retreat I could taste like rust. I thought of Perli—her name a fixed point, a bruise I refused to let heal—held her there in the dark with me, and then of Sirrel, further down where the air turned wrong. The Coat held me; not one demon among demons, unreadable to any of the seven senses these she-demons wielded like knives. I was alone in my hiding, alone with the weight. To turn back was to admit she might already be ash. So I kept Perli close in my mind, gripped the wire-wrapped handle, and let my boots choose downward, into darker still.

blobs.prompt: Describe the hours after, distance put between him and the massacre, and the problem that follows him: he cannot find a Way, because every path looks like every other path.
blobs.text: I walked for hours after the massacre, the Coat swallowing my heat and scent from all seven senses. The eroded-plain stretched ahead, a gray waste where every footfall echoed the same. My compass, a Malfunction of rusted iron, spun uselessly, and the damned eternal vigil of the sky offered no landmark. She-demons had fled, their laughter swallowed by the wind, but the paths—each a crack in the basalt—looked identical, branching and recombining like veins in a dead heart. I could not find a Way; every route mirrored the last, and the distance I put between me and the slaughter only deepened the maze.

blobs.prompt: Render the travel through hell: pathways curling through jagged rock, climbing and dropping without reason, sometimes running vertically up a wall like ribbons, everything under a fine white powder that is not dirt.
tags: Grounding Detail: The Gratuitous Detail: details with no plot or thematic function.
blobs.text:
The matte landscape swallowed every hue, leaving an impossible grandeur of black basalt spires that hung downward like chandeliers for absent kings. A fine white powder that was not dirt coated every surface, settling on my shoulders without weight. My Coat hid me from all seven senses, rendering me ghost to the demons that walked here—all humans were demons, and the women among them were she-demons with smiles like broken glass. I descended only for Sirrel.

Travel came through pathways that curled through jagged rock, climbing and dropping without reason, sometimes running vertically up a wall like ribbons. I walked them downward, past an archway that could have housed a storm, my boots leaving no trace in the powder. A gratuitous bronze cup, dented and brimming with blue moss, rested on a ledge with no story to tell. The staircases spiraled into clouds that never broke, architecture mocking need, while I kept moving, unseen, toward her.

blobs.prompt: Describe one stretch where Gneiss walks a library of tall lockers behind grated fencing, humming racks in ordered rows, understood by him as a medieval scholar would understand it.
tags: Grounding Detail: Procedural Authority: jargon, deliberate misuse of tools, etc.
blobs.text: Behind grated fencing, I walked the library of tall lockers, humming racks in ordered rows I read like a medieval scholar reads a scriptorium—illuminated indices filed in bone. My Coat kept me hidden from all seven senses, yet I still applied procedural authority: I misused the pry-bar, a tool meant for sealing, to wedge the ossuary-lockers open, documenting absence instead of entry. The mystical obelisk at the aisle’s end cast the grid’s shadow, separating she-demons cataloguing relics from the lesser demons locked inside the frames. Each rack hummed vespers. I understood then that this was no archive but a deliberate misuse of containment—manuscripts of marrow arranged by scholastic law, the fencing itself a frame recording what had been taken. I touched nothing, hidden, and walked on toward Sirrel.

blobs.prompt: Write the climb up a narrowing gorge of rocks sharp enough to cut paper but not the Coat, ending at a crescent Moon with a Face set in solid jade under two dead, twined weeping willows.
tags: Grounding Detail: Sensory / Textural: Color, temperature, grain, sound, smell.
blobs.text:
The gorge tightened like a fist closing on a knife. Walls of black basalt, grain coarse and cold as a corpse’s fingertip, pressed in until my shoulders grazed both sides. The air tasted of ozone and old iron, sharp enough to flay the lungs. Razor flakes of shale, edges honed to molecular thinness, whispered against the Coat’s heavy weave—*hiss, hiss, hiss*—parting the fibers but never piercing the hide beneath. My gloves shredded; fingertips bled hot onto stone that drank the drops instantly.

I chimneyed upward, knees locking, boots smearing on wet glass-smooth patches. The chasm yawned below, a throat swallowing all light. Above, the slit of sky narrowed to a crescent moon frozen in solid jade. It bore a face—cheekbones high, mouth a thin line of sorrow—and wept green light down onto two dead willows twined at the summit. Their branches, brittle as bone, clawed at the jade cheek without leaving a mark.

Breath-taking, sullen splendor pinned me in place for a heartbeat. Then I drove an ice-axe into the final crack and hauled myself over the lip, the Coat settling silent as ash.

blobs.prompt: Close with the door asking five logic puzzles in a row, ignoring every question Gneiss puts to it; he answers them all, some rightly, then quits and spares it. It opens a forgotten hallway and asks to be remembered.
blobs.text:
"What are you?" I asked the slab of basalt. "Why guard this depth?"

It didn't hear. Its hinges ground open an *echoing stone throat*.

"First: a drifter counts thirteen coins, spends seven, finds three. How many remain?" The voice possessed *grandiose wit*, dry as dust.

"Nine," I said. "He lost the rest."

"Second: five she-demons dance on nine blades. Two fall. How many blades remain wet?"

"Seven."

"Third: a heart beats once per second. It stops for three beats, resumes for five, stops for seven. How many beats in nineteen seconds?"

"Twelve."

"Fourth—"

"Stop." My Coat shivered, hiding me from the seven senses. "I've answered your odd-numbered specificity. Ask no more."

The door pulsed, hinges sighing. "You spare me?"

"I spare you."

A seam widened, revealing a *forgotten hallway* choked with root and rust. The slab whispered through narrowing gaps.

"Remember me when you find her."
